Testing variable and value labels

Source: vignettes/label_test.Rmd
label_test.Rmd

Two functions check the labels of a field data delivery against the PV (Programmiervorlage):

  • label_test() checks the variable labels (vb-tag),
  • value_label_test() checks the value labels, i.e. the codes and their labels (we-tag).

One call checks all variables of a module. This vignette explains how the tests work, so that you can judge their output. The first part is about variable labels, the second about value labels.

Usage 

library(nepstest)

T_26ET  <- haven::read_dta("26ET.dta")
pv_26ET <- read_pv("NEPS_B180_SC6_EP_26ET_V2_2_20250312.docx")

label_test(T_26ET, pv_26ET)
value_label_test(T_26ET, pv_26ET)

The data must be read with haven::read_dta(), so that every variable carries its label as the attribute label. Several PVs can be read at once with read_pv(c("PV_26ET.docx", "PV_27AL.docx")).

Variable labels

label_test() runs in four steps.

Step 1: Reading the PV

read_pv() reads all tables of the docx file. Every table row that contains at least one tag (--va:, --vb:, …) becomes one item. The text of a tag runs from its tag line to the next tag line or to --end--. The first column of the table is kept as the item number (e.g. 26122 or 23103P1).

The result has one column per tag, so it can also be used for other purposes, e.g. to look up an ef-tag:

pv_26ET[pv_26ET$item %in% "26181b", c("va", "ef")]

Step 2: Expected label per variable

The internal function pv_var_labels() derives from the va- and vb-tags which label each variable should have in the data. It is not exported, but you can call it with nepstest::: to see the expected labels:

labels_26ET <- nepstest:::pv_var_labels(pv_26ET)

Markers in front of the variable name ([ZS], [HILF], …) and [MF] at the start of the vb-tag are removed. Items with a single variable get the vb-tag as it is. Items whose va-tag lists several variables are split into one row per variable. The survey institute builds those labels as text before the list + the part for this variable + text after the list, and drops the brackets and slashes:

Item type va-tag vb-tag Expected label (example)
Date etstdat (etstm / etstj) Startdatum (-monat/-jahr) Erwerbsepisode etstm: Startdatum Monat Erwerbsepisode
Date etentdat1 (etent1m / etent1j) Datum (Monat/Jahr) der Entfristung etent1j: Datum Jahr der Entfristung
Multiple choice etintro1a (etintro1a1 / ... ) Interviewerangabe bei Widerspruch (Berufsangabe / …) etintro1a1: Interviewerangabe bei Widerspruch Berufsangabe
List with commas h_etzeit (h_etzeit1, h_etzeit2, ...) Zeitarbeit andauernder Erwerbsepisoden (h_etzeit1, h_etzeit2, …) h_etzeit1: Zeitarbeit andauernder Erwerbsepisoden h_etzeit1

Details:

  • The list is the first bracket in the vb-tag that contains slashes or commas and has as many parts as the va-tag has variables. If there is no such bracket, the first bracket with slashes or commas is used.
  • The parts are assigned to the variables in order. A leading hyphen is removed and date parts are capitalized (-monat becomes Monat).
  • More variables than parts: multiple choice items often have extra variables for “verweigert” and “weiß nicht” that are not in the vb-tag, e.g. ts2352 (ts23525 / ... / ts23529) with only three parts in the vb-tag. The first variables get the parts in order, the label of the remaining ones is taken from their line in the we-tag (ts23528: verweigert gives “Sondervergütung verweigert”). The output mentions every item where this rule was used.
  • No list at all: if the va-tag has several variables but the vb-tag has no bracket with slashes or commas (e.g. vb “Trennungsdatum”), no label is derived. The variable gets the status “unclear” (see below) and has to be checked by hand.

Step 3: Matching data and PV variables

Every variable of the data is matched to a PV variable by name:

  • Same name: matched.
  • Loop variables with a suffix like _1, _2 are matched to the PV variable without the suffix.
  • Variables whose names match a pattern in ignore are skipped. Default: duration variables (duration$) and variables ending in _e.

Variables that are only in the data or only in the PV are listed as a NOTE. They do not make the test fail, use var_exists() if a missing variable should be an error.

Step 4: Comparing the labels

Each matched variable gets one status:

Status Meaning Test fails?
ok Identical (apart from blanks). no
format Differs only in brackets, slashes, hyphens, quotes, colons, commas or upper/lower case. no
truncated The data label is cut off at Stata’s limit of 80 characters but otherwise identical. no
item_ref The data label refers to other items by item number where the PV uses the variable name, e.g. a preload with “(23110)” in the data and “(bvnr)” in the PV. Only accepted if the item number belongs to exactly that variable in the PV. no
unclear No expected label could be derived from the PV (see step 2). Listed with the reason and the data label. no
mismatch Any other difference. Both labels are printed. yes
missing_label The variable has no label in the data. yes

If any variable has the status mismatch or missing_label, the function stops with an error at the end, like the other test functions of the package.

Reading the output

A run with one wrong label looks like this:

Comparing the variable labels of 32 variable(s) in T23_Full with the PV.
ERROR - 1 variable label(s) differ from the PV:
  bvmn     (item 23109)
    data: Maßnahmeart Weiterbildung
    PV:   Maßnahmeart
NOTE: 3 label(s) differ only in brackets, slashes, hyphens, punctuation or case. Use show_format = TRUE to list them.
NOTE: 7 label(s) refer to items by item number where the PV uses the variable name (the numbers match the PV). Use show_format = TRUE to list them.
NOTE: 1 variable(s) are in the data but not in the PV: caseid
Error: label_test failed. Please inspect the above labels.

Useful arguments:

  • show_format = TRUE also prints the labels with the status format and item_ref, to check them by eye.
  • stop_on_fail = FALSE prints the same output but does not stop. The function then returns the full comparison table, which can be filtered:
res <- label_test(T_26ET, pv_26ET, stop_on_fail = FALSE)
res[res$status == "mismatch", ]
attr(res, "only_in_pv")
  • show_unmatched = FALSE hides the lists of variables that are only in the data or only in the PV.

Value labels

value_label_test() works like label_test(): the PV is read with read_pv(), the expected codes are derived per variable, data and PV variables are matched by name (including loop suffixes and ignore), and then the codes are compared. In the data, the value labels of a variable are a named vector (attribute labels, as set by haven::read_dta()): the values are the codes, the names are the labels.

Expected codes per variable

The internal function pv_value_labels() reads the we-tag line by line. You can call it with nepstest::: to see the expected codes:

values_26ET <- nepstest:::pv_value_labels(pv_26ET)
values_26ET[values_26ET$var == "etbs", ]
Line in the we-tag Example Gives
Code 1: Arbeiter/in code 1 “Arbeiter/in”
Code with a condition if (h_etauto = 0) 5: Selbstständige/r code 5 “Selbstständige/r”, the condition is removed
Buttons BUTTONS: verweigert (-97), weiß nicht (-98) codes -97 and -98
Button with a condition [if h_panel = 0] bis heute (-5) code -5 “bis heute”
Interviewer hint <<z. B. Ärztin/Arzt, ...>> nothing
List [Länderliste], [Gemeindeliste] the codes come from a list that is not in the PV, see list below
Open answer, date field OFFEN: ____, Monat ____ Jahr _____ nothing

Grouped items:

  • Multiple choice (the we-tag has lines like ts23525 1: ... or [0: nicht genannt]): every variable of the item gets the codes in square brackets, usually 0: nicht genannt and 1: genannt. The texts of the single answers and their conditions do not matter, they are the variable labels.
  • Dates: the month variable gets the codes of the buttons plus the season codes from the in-tag (21=Jahresanfang/Winter, 24=Frühjahr/Ostern, …). The year variable only gets the codes of the buttons.
  • Other lists (e.g. h_etzeit1, h_etzeit2, …): every variable gets the same codes.

If a code appears several times with different texts (under different conditions), each of these texts is accepted.

Comparing the codes

For every variable, all codes of the PV and of the data are compared:

Status Meaning Test fails?
ok Code in PV and data, labels identical (apart from blanks). no
format Labels differ only in brackets, slashes, hyphens, quotes, colons, commas or upper/lower case. no
fill_in The PV label is only a fill-in like <h_etarta1>, so only the code is checked. no
list The item takes its codes from a list that is not in the PV (e.g. [Länderliste]), so codes in the data that are not in the PV are not checked. They are counted in a NOTE. The buttons of the item (e.g. -96 “Land nicht in Liste”) are still checked. no
mismatch The labels differ otherwise. yes
missing_in_data The code is in the PV, but has no label in the data. yes
not_in_pv The code has a label in the data, but is not in the PV. yes

Variables without codes in the PV (e.g. episode numbers) must not have value labels in the data, otherwise each of their codes is not_in_pv. Character variables (open answers) cannot carry value labels in Stata and are skipped.

The output lists the differences per variable:

Comparing the value labels of 98 variable(s) in T26_Full with the PV.
NOTE: 9 character variable(s) were skipped (open answers have no value labels).
ERROR - value labels of 2 variable(s) differ from the PV:
  etbs  (item 26111)
       3: missing in data (PV: "Beamtin/Beamter, auch Richter/in, außer Soldat/in")
       9: not in PV (data: "Beamtin/Beamter, auch Richter/in, außer Soldat/in")
  etselb1  (item 26113)
       2: data: "Landwirtin"  PV: "Selbstständige/r Landwirt/in"
Error: value_label_test failed. Please inspect the above value labels.

show_format = TRUE and stop_on_fail = FALSE work like in label_test().

Limits

  • The rules describe how the survey institute builds labels in the deliveries checked so far (26ET, 23BV). If a module uses a different convention, the affected variables show up as errors, and the rule has to be added to pv_var_labels() (R/labels.R) or pv_value_labels() (R/value_labels.R).
  • The PV must be a docx file.
